set.pl: Northern Pacific main line between Wadena Junction and Bluffton; the main dig was near the Peter Nelson home 'a mile on this side of Bluffton' (Wadena Pioneer Journal, 10 May 1906); farm not yet on a plat (ring 1.5 km)
set.st: In June 1905 J. Buchan, about 70, of Pine River, who had worked on the Northern Pacific construction when the road was built through Wadena, was searching for several thousand dollars in gold he said was buried at one of the construction-gang camps. He carried blueprints of the right of way marking the camp sites, given him by a friend on his death-bed. He first tried east of the town and failed, then placed the cache west of Wadena, between the town and the junction, while lodging at a farm three miles east of the village. Nothing is reported found. Buchan gave up in mid-June 1905 after visiting every old camp site on his charts. The paper recalled an older tradition: years before, a stranger had dug on the right of way near Verndale and at an old camp near the Wing River for money cached about 1873, at the Jay Cooke failure, by a sub-contractor said to be Cooke's brother-in-law, who died suddenly and poor. In May 1906 J. M. Day of Pillager, with all of Buchan's maps (witness trees, hills, cuts), renewed the search along the track between Wadena Junction and Bluffton; Buchan's main dig had been near Peter Nelson's home a mile east of Bluffton, where Nelson and his son helped dig and struck iron that proved to be an old plowshare. The outcome is not reported. Pin is a mile east of Bluffton on the line, not the dig.
set.t: Railroad right of way and private farmland: ask first. The Peter Nelson farm a mile east of Bluffton (c.1906 Otter Tail or Wadena plat) is the place to narrow it.
set.tovw: Lead grade D: three local issues and a Duluth special report two searches with the camp blueprints and a dig near Bluffton that found a plowshare; the gold rests on a death-bed story and no recovery is reported.
